    4. Greedily select the candidate that has the *smallest* maximum dot product (but still <= 2).
       This prioritizes points that are "less conflicting" with the existing set,
       potentially allowing more points to be added later.
       Tie-breaking is done lexicographically based on the point's tuple representation.
    5. When a point is added, efficiently update the max dot product values for all remaining candidates,
       removing any that become invalid. Vectorized NumPy operations are used for speed.

    random.seed(42)
